title: Backdoor Subtlety vs Attacker Capability Replicated Across Open Attackers

original_idea.body:
# Backdoor Subtlety vs Attacker Capability Replicated Across Open Attackers

**Problem:** Control Tax found, surprisingly, that stronger attacker models do not necessarily create subtler backdoors (monitoring stayed consistent across attacker capability). This counterintuitive result deserves independent replication on a different attacker pool.

**Direction:** Replicate the attacker-capability-vs-backdoor-subtlety experiment using a diverse set of open attacker models of varying size on the APPS task, holding the monitor fixed. Measure detection AUC per attacker and test whether monitorability really stays flat with attacker capability, or whether the trend differs for open models.

**Why it matters:** Whether stronger AIs produce harder-to-catch attacks is foundational to control's long-run viability. Independently confirming or refuting the 'flat monitorability' result with open models is high-value, lab-free reproducibility.

**Relevant context:** Control Tax (arXiv 2506.05296): monitoring performance consistent across diverse attackers; stronger models don't make subtler backdoors. Provides balanced APPS backdoor dataset.
